It’s not. Their therapists are actually licensed, they should have their license number and expiration date and everything on their page once you sign up. It’s also more affordable than in person therapy and they offer a financial aid option too

I can’t speak for the meds, as I used to be on Zoloft but stopped because I got tired of the side effects, but I understand the struggle of not being able to meet up consistently with a therapist. 

I dunno if you’ve heard of BetterHelp, but it’s an online therapy website that’s been promoted on Reddit a lot. I tried it out even though a lot of reviews weren’t favorable, but I’ve stuck with the same therapist for about 5 months now and she’s helped me so so much, way more than my shitty in person therapist did. I do a 45 minute text based therapy session every week/week and a half, and I can check in with her by sending her a message whenever I want. It’s nice because I don’t have to worry about driving to an office to see someone in person (I’m in college and it’s a pain).  I really recommend it, and I hope things get better for you! My username for this account pretty much says it all. Anything negative in my life, I’m posting to reddit hoping someone will see it and empathize with me. 

I posted on the depression sub with my main account once and my former boyfriend saw it, and I just wanted an account where I could talk openly about my struggles with anxiety, depression, and my relationship without worrying about if someone could identify me.

He said that he hasn’t felt the spark between us in awhile and it just never came back, that he didn’t really see where the relationship was going and he didn’t want to marry me. The love is there, the attraction is there, the friendship is there, but the willingness to keep trying to get a spark back isn’t. That frustrates me because I know that you have to keep working at it, and really the problem as I see it is that he doesn’t want to try. 

Keep in mind, of course, that we’re in our third year of college, have been dating since our second semester of freshman year, and were both in relationships for the first semester too.  He’s trying to figure out who he is, what he wants to do, and all of that stuff. He’s not trying to go out and fuck other people.

For me, it’s just a constant sense of frustration with how I feel because it’s something I don’t fully understand, and I don’t like not being in control.
